```markdown
**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-07**

- **Member name:** Emerson Delgado
- **Member ID:** W727121486
- **Reference number:** POC-A93FE7E3B5-95850
- **Requested service denied:** Lower back (lumbar) fusion, CPT 22612
- **Governing policy:** Lumbar Spinal Fusion, Surgery Policy No. 187 (SUR187) — https://blue.regence.com/trgmedpol/surgery/sur187.pdf
- **Appeal deadline stated in the notice:** must be received by 2027-02-03

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing Regence BlueShield's denial of prior authorization for my lumbar fusion (CPT 22612), issued on 2026-08-07 under reference number POC-A93FE7E3B5-95850. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery my surgeon, Reyes, MD (orthopedic surgery), has documented that I need.

The denial does not say that my surgery fails any particular medical criterion. It says the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am writing because the prior authorization packet already contains the clinical facts that correspond to the criteria published in the plan's own policy, and I am setting them out below, point by point, so that the plan can see them together in one place.

I am relying on the plan's own published medical policy, Lumbar Spinal Fusion, Surgery Policy No. 187 (SUR187). Every quotation below is taken word for word from that policy. Where I describe my own care, I am describing what my records state.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. The policy's spinal stenosis pathway.** The policy provides for coverage of:

> "Spinal stenosis when all of the following Criteria are met:"

That sentence introduces a list of conditions. I have been given only some of the items on that list, and I address each of the ones I have below. I ask the plan to identify in writing which specific criteria from this section it applied to my request, and which of them it considered unsupported.

**2. Symptoms.** The policy requires:

> "Neurogenic claudication or radicular pain; and"

My records document neurogenic claudication on examination, along with diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes. I have had 14 months of progressive pain in my lower back and legs that is not relieved by rest. I cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop, and sitting relieves it.

**3. Imaging.** The policy requires:

> "Documented central, lateral recess, or foraminal stenosis, with or without disc protrusion/herniation, facet arthropathy or facet cyst, or ligamentum flavum hypertrophy on MRI or other advanced imaging consistent with the individual's symptoms"

My MRI of the lumbar spine on 2026-05-29 documents severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina. That finding is central stenosis on MRI, and it matches the symptoms described above — claudication that comes on with standing and walking and eases with sitting.

**4. Spondylolisthesis / instability.** The policy requires:

> "Spondylolisthesis at a level (L1-S1) to be included in the fusion demonstrated on x-rays, CT, or MRI or there is a high likelihood of post-operative instability due to severity of stenosis and extent of decompression/facetectomy"

My imaging of 2026-05-29 — MRI together with flexion-extension radiographs — documents grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension. L4-L5 is within the L1-S1 range named in the policy, and the finding was demonstrated on both x-rays and MRI.

**5. Functional impairment.** The policy requires:

> "There is either clinical documentation of significant functional impairment or disability, or objective measurement of severe disability using the Oswestry Disability Index tool"

This criterion is satisfied by either route. My chart contains clinical documentation of my functional limitation: I cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop. That limitation has been present and progressive for 14 months.

**6. Conservative nonoperative therapy.** The policy requires:

> "There is clinical documentation that a minimum of three months of conservative nonoperative therapy failed to adequately treat the individual's current symptoms including one or more of the following:"

My records document a course of conservative nonoperative therapy longer than three months that did not adequately control my symptoms:

- **NSAIDs for 4 months**, with inadequate relief.
- **Supervised physical therapy**, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, from 2026-05-07 to 2026-07-16 — 10 weeks, 16 visits completed — documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-18**, which gave 4 weeks of partial relief and then wore off.

Within that same section, the policy names, among the qualifying items:

> "Physical therapy or professionally-directed therapeutic independent home exercise program unless contraindication is clearly documented"

and

> "Two or more of the following treatment modalities have been attempted:"

followed by, among others:

> "Prescription anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics, or prescription strength doses of OTC anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics"

and

> "Injection therapy of epidural or facet joint implicated pain sources in the area of concern, including but not limited to epidural steroid injection, medial branch block, radiofrequency ablation, selective nerve root injection, or discogram"

I completed supervised physical therapy, as described above. I also attempted two of the listed treatment modalities: anti-inflammatory medication for four months, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-18. Neither adequately treated my current symptoms.

The policy also lists, in this same section:

> "Documented cauda equina syndrome, progressive motor loss, or subjective worsening of symptoms during a course of conservative management when clearly documented in the medical record"

My records state that my pain in the lower back and legs has been progressive over 14 months. My records also state that I have no bowel or bladder dysfunction. I am not claiming a diagnosis my chart does not contain; I am pointing out that my imaging documents severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina, and that my symptoms worsened rather than improved while I was pursuing the conservative care described above.

**7. Nicotine.** The policy requires:

> "The individual is nicotine-free OR there is clinical documentation that the individual has been abstinent from nicotine use for at least six weeks prior to planned procedure based on attestation or laboratory results (cotinine or nicotine levels)"

My records state that I am a non-smoker. My records also state that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, and a BMI of 29.

**8. Sections of the policy that do not apply to me.** For completeness, the policy also addresses other clinical situations — for example:

> "Spinal fracture with instability or neural compression"

> "Spinal repair surgery for dislocation, tumor, or infection (including abscess, osteomyelitis, discitis, or fungal infection) when debridement is necessary and the extent of the debridement to help eradicate the infection creates or could create an unstable spine"

> "Single- or multi-session (staged) fusion for severe, progressive idiopathic scoliosis (i.e., lumbar or thoracolumbar) with Cobb angle greater than 40 degrees"

> "Isthmic spondylolisthesis when all of the following Criteria are met: 1. Either congenital (Wiltse type I) or acquired pars defect (Wiltse II), documented on x-ray"

My request does not rest on any of these. My documented diagnosis is grade I **degenerative** spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with severe central stenosis, so the spinal stenosis section of the policy is the one that applies to my situation. If the review was conducted against one of these other sections, that would explain a mismatch, and I ask that my request be re-reviewed against the spinal stenosis criteria instead.

## A note on the quoted language

The excerpts above are the portions of Lumbar Spinal Fusion, Surgery Policy No. 187 (SUR187) that I have in front of me, quoted exactly. Several of them end in a colon and introduce further conditions that I have not seen in full. I am not guessing at what those additional conditions say, and I am not stating any number, duration, grade or threshold as the plan's requirement unless it appears in the language above. Anything in this letter that is not inside quotation marks is my own description of my records, not the plan's policy.

## What I am asking the plan to do

1. Reconsider and overturn the denial dated 2026-08-07 and authorize CPT 22612 as requested by Reyes, MD.
2. If any document is still considered missing, please tell me and my surgeon's office specifically **which document and which criterion** it relates to, so it can be sent promptly. The denial states only that the submission was incomplete, and I cannot supply a record without knowing which one is wanted.
3. Please identify the specific criteria from Lumbar Spinal Fusion, Surgery Policy No. 187 (SUR187) that were applied to my request and the basis on which each was found unmet.
4. Please have this appeal reviewed by a physician with training in spine surgery.
5. Please send me a copy of the full medical policy and the clinical review criteria used in my case.

I am attaching the records referenced above for the reviewer's convenience:

- MRI lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiograph reports dated 2026-05-29
- Physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-05-07 to 2026-07-16 (16 visits)
- Procedure note for the corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-18
- Office notes from Reyes, MD, including the surgical recommendation
- [Any additional records my surgeon's office includes]

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-03. I am submitting it using the appeal form for Washington from the Regence member appeals page at regence.com/member/members/member-appeals, to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also submit by fax at 1-888-496-1542, or call the number on the back of my member ID card with questions.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. My surgeon has documented that this operation is needed, and I would like to get back to standing and walking without stopping every ten minutes.

Sincerely,

**Emerson Delgado**
Member ID: W727121486
Reference number: POC-A93FE7E3B5-95850
[Signature]
[Date]

Enclosures: as listed above
cc: Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
```
